metadata.note: The Kanona and Prattsburg(h) Railway, Steuben County, New York: an independent, locally owned 11.4-mile steam branch from the Erie Rochester Division at Kanona north to Prattsburgh, opened 1889. Sold at foreclosure in 1917 and reorganised as the Prattsburgh Railway Corporation. Passenger (mixed-train) service drawn 1889-1929; freight and express continued to 1959 and is not drawn (Rule 1). Spelling 'Prattsburg'/'Prattsburgh' varies by source and era. Research report: research/branches/kanona_and_prattsburgh_railway.txt.
sources: https://theclio.com/entry/184350 -- Clio, Wheeler Center Depot (opening Oct 1889; passenger end 9 Mar 1929; last train 29 Sept 1959)

https://crookedlakereview.com/articles/67_100/67oct1993/67palmer.html -- Richard F. Palmer, Crooked Lake Review, Oct 1993, quoting a 1939 50th-anniversary article (Sept/Oct 1889 opening; 1917 foreclosure and reorganisation; passengers discontinued 1929)
https://www.wgpfoundation.org/historic-markers/wheeler-station/ -- William G. Pomeroy Foundation, Wheeler Station marker
https://www.branchline.uk/jfpdf/newyorkstaterrs4.pdf -- Fowler, New York State railroads part 4, table 222 (stations and mileages; 1895 Peoples Guide)
research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt -- Official Guide Feb 1952, Prattsburgh Railway Corporation: 11.4 mi, freight and express only, Aug 1951
metadata.operator_split: Split at 1917 into two features with identical geometry (CLAUDE.md Rule 4): the 1917 foreclosure sale created a new operating company, the Prattsburgh Railway Corporation, so 1889-1917 is drawn in the Kanona and Prattsburg Railway's colour and 1917-1929 in the Prattsburgh Railway's. No Erie lease or operation at any time.
metadata.freight_only_audit: Not drawn: 9 Mar 1929 - 29 Sept 1959 freight and express only (and the 1961 auction). Segments end at the 1929 passenger end.
not_yet_sourced: Primary source for the 9 March 1929 passenger end: only secondary sources (Clio; Palmer's reproduction of a 1939 article) found. A Steuben County newspaper 'last train' story (nyshistoricnewspapers.org, fultonhistory.com) would give a primary citation.
Month of the 1917 foreclosure sale and reorganisation (Palmer gives the year only); the feature split is drawn at 1917.
Headway and average speed: no public timetable found for 1889-1929; both are estimates.
Opening month conflict: Sept 1889 (Palmer, fair traffic to a temporary railhead) vs Oct 1889 (Clio) - same year.
Organisation date conflict: 1886 (Wheeler station marker) vs 1888 (Palmer) - pre-opening, does not affect drawn years.
Whether passengers rode freight trains after 9 Mar 1929: no evidence either way; not drawn.

properties.speed_source: estimated: an 11.4-mile steam branch with mixed trains, a 258-ft climb toward Prattsburgh and seven flag stops; no timetable or running time found - unsourced
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap (ODbL): ways 1515730995, 1515730994, 49095598, 902712162, 902712161 fetched 2026-10-18 from the OSM API (Overpass mirrors timing out); surrounding rail graph from Overpass (overpass.kumi.systems). Routed with opstrace.py Kanona (Erie junction) - Wheeler - Prattsburgh, Douglas-Peucker 8 m, trim_reversals. No old_railway_operator tag exists for this road in OSM (probed 'Kanona|Prattsburg').
properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced throughout from OpenStreetMap; no approximated (straight-line) legs. The whole line survives in OSM as railway=abandoned named 'Kanona and Prattsburgh Railroad', a continuous chain Kanona -> Prattsburgh (ways 1515730995, 1515730994, 49095598, 902712162, 902712161); the opstrace.py route ran entirely on that chain (max deviation 0 m from the raw chain). 11.56 mi traced (11.57 mi before Douglas-Peucker 8 m + trim_reversals) against 11.4 mi documented (Official Guide Feb 1952; Fowler table 222; Palmer) and 11.44 mi (Clio) - about 1.5% long. Kanona end is the K&P way's first node, which is shared with the abandoned Erie Rochester Division way 1299059965 (the Erie connection; the K&P used the Erie's Kanona station). Prattsburgh end is the end of way 902712161 at Prattsburgh village; the Prattsburgh yard/turntable stubs (ways 902712170, 902712157-60) are not drawn. Alignment era: no later realignment is known - a single alignment for the line's whole life, so the drawing is of the line's own era.

segments.note: Kanona (connection with the Erie Rochester Division, using the Erie station) - Jordan's - Marshall's - Wheeler - Renchan's - Dinehart's - Stickney's - Bean's Station - Prattsburgh, 11.4 mi. Opened 1889: Palmer (Crooked Lake Review, Oct 1993, quoting a 1939 50th-anniversary newspaper article) has passengers carried in Sept 1889 to a temporary railhead about a mile short of Prattsburg for the county fair, line completed Oct 1889; Clio gives 'opening day in October of 1889' - same year either way. Steam from the first day (4-4-0 No. 1 'Old Huldey', Pittsburgh 1889, built the line with work trains); trains ran as small mixed consists, which count as passenger service. Segment ends at the 1917 foreclosure sale and reorganisation as the Prattsburgh Railway Corporation (Palmer; month not found) - a change of operating company, not an end of service, which continues in the Prattsburgh Railway feature. Independent throughout; never leased to or operated by the Erie. headway_min 720 (about two trains a day each way) is an ESTIMATE: no timetable for the road was found, and the research report says only that a mixed train once or twice daily is plausible but unproven.
sources: Segment-level: 1889 opening from Clio (Wheeler Center Depot entry) and Palmer, Crooked Lake Review Oct 1993; 1917 foreclosure/reorganisation from Palmer (month not established). Stations confirmed by 1895 per Fowler table 222 (1895 Peoples Guide). Headway and speed NOT sourced - estimates.

segments.note: Same 11.4-mi Kanona - Prattsburgh line and steam operation, now run by the Prattsburgh Railway Corporation, formed by 171 local subscribers after the 1917 foreclosure sale (Palmer; month not found). Passenger service ended 9 March 1929 (Clio, which supplies the day; Palmer's 1939 text: 'Passenger service was discontinued in 1929'). Context only, not drawn: the road then carried freight and express only - the Feb 1952 Official Guide lists it as 'Freight and express service only' - until the last train on 29 Sept 1959 (Clio, Wheeler marker); property auctioned 1961. headway_min 720 (about two trains a day each way) is an ESTIMATE: no timetable for the road was found, and the research report says only that a mixed train once or twice daily is plausible but unproven.
sources: Segment-level: 1917 reorganisation from Palmer, Crooked Lake Review Oct 1993 (month not established); passenger end 9 March 1929 from Clio, corroborated by Palmer's 1939 newspaper text. Feb 1952 Official Guide (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt) confirms freight-only in 1951 only - not used as the end date. Headway and speed NOT sourced - estimates.
